title: Are Multi-Model Discussions More Honest Than Single Models Under Pressure?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Downgraded. Multiple 2024-2025 papers directly study sycophancy in multi-agent debate, finding it does not reliably reduce sycophancy and can introduce new failure modes.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Two API calls per question (Model A answers, Model B critiques, Model A revises) is simple to implement. Comparing with single-model baseline is basic. Accessible to beginners with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tight experiment: single-model vs. two-model debate on a sycophancy battery. Clear deliverable: accuracy comparison. Achievable in 30 hours. Doubles API costs but stays within medium compute.

novelty.reasoning: 'Peacemaker or Troublemaker: How Sycophancy Shapes Multi-Agent Debate' (arXiv:2509.23055, 2025) directly studies how sycophancy affects multi-agent debate outcomes. 'Talk Isn't Always Cheap: Understanding Failure Modes in Multi-Agent Debate' (arXiv:2509.05396, 2025) documents that agent disagreement rate decreases as debate progresses, correlated with performance degradation. 'Measuring and Mitigating Identity Bias in Multi-Agent Debate via Anonymization' (arXiv:2510.07517, 2025) examines identity-based yielding in debate. 'Should we be going MAD?' (ICML 2024) finds multi-agent debate does not consistently outperform single agents. The proposed experiment — comparing single-model vs. multi-model honesty under sycophancy pressure — is directly addressed by these 2024-2025 papers.
